label: Peak DC fast-charge rate sustained only briefly
description: Manufacturers advertise the peak instantaneous DC fast-charge rate (e.g., '250 kW Supercharging'). In real-world charging sessions, the peak is achieved only between roughly 5–22% state of charge, sustained for ~5–6 minutes, then tapers significantly. The advertised number rarely reflects the average rate during a real 10–80% charge.
regulatory_basis: No regulatory framework. Charging-curve disclosure is voluntary. Some EU regulations require WLTP-derived charging time labels, but US has none.
consumer_harm: Trip planning based on advertised peak underestimates total charge time. A 'charges in 18 minutes' claim that requires arrival at <10% SOC and a perfectly preconditioned battery does not reflect typical road-trip experience.
